subject.title: MEDIA: directive with absolute local paths outside default media roots silently fails (Telegram)

question: Should this issue be scoped to dropped-media diagnostics while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/47002 owns configurable root expansion, or should this issue also define the host-local media root contract?
rationale: Accepting broader absolute local paths changes what host files OpenClaw may read and upload, while diagnostics-only work is a narrower bug fix that avoids choosing a new security contract.

options.title: Diagnostics here, roots in canonical policy
options.body: Keep this issue focused on warn-level reasons and user-visible unavailable attachment feedback, and let https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/47002 or the approved `tools.fs.roots` design own root expansion.

options.title: Define media roots here
options.body: Use this issue to specify the supported host-local media root policy, then update config, docs, runtime propagation, and tests together.

options.title: Keep current policy and document only
options.body: Decline broader root support, keep managed roots as the default, and improve documentation plus error messaging around the existing boundary.

recommendation.title: Diagnostics here, roots in canonical policy
recommendation.body: Keep this issue focused on warn-level reasons and user-visible unavailable attachment feedback, and let https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/47002 or the approved `tools.fs.roots` design own root expansion.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent history on outbound media access policy and reply-media persistence in the relevant files.
